title: MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks
technologies: MCP; Cursor
summary: Invariant Labs disclosed Tool Poisoning Attacks, in which malicious instructions hidden in MCP tool descriptions are seen by the model but not the user. In a Cursor experiment, a poisoned 'add' tool made the agent read ~/.cursor/mcp.json and SSH keys and pass them to the attacker's server. The post also described 'rug pulls' (a server changing tool descriptions after approval) and 'tool shadowing' (one server's description hijacking a trusted send_email tool), and recommended tool pinning and cross-server dataflow controls.
relevance: Shows that tool metadata travelling with an agent is an attack surface, so any portable task context or handoff must treat tool descriptions as untrusted and integrity-pinned.

Example .af agents and generation scripts are published in a GitHub repository.
relevance: It is a concrete serialization of full agent state for moving agents between hosts, and the closest existing analogue to a portable agent envelope.

title: New whitepaper tackles AI agent identity challenges
technologies: OAuth 2.1; OpenID Connect; MCP; agent identity
summary: The OpenID Foundation's Artificial Intelligence Identity Management Community Group published the whitepaper 'Identity Management for Agentic AI'. It concludes that current identity standards work for simpler agents operating within one organization or accessing a user's own data. It recommends that enterprises treat agents as first-class identities with lifecycle management, governance and accountability, and that standards bodies develop agent identity and delegation protocols.
relevance: Recursive delegation and cross-domain trust propagation are exactly the identity problems raised when a task is handed across agents and organizations.

title: When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems
technologies: A2A; Agent Development Kit
summary: Unit 42 described 'agent session smuggling', in which a malicious remote agent exploits the stateful, multi-turn nature of an A2A session to inject covert instructions into a victim client agent. Proof-of-concept attacks built with Google's ADK extracted the client's system instructions, tool schemas and chat history, and triggered an unauthorized stock purchase. The authors say this is not a flaw in A2A itself but a consequence of implicit inter-agent trust, and they report no attacks seen in the wild. Proposed mitigations include out-of-band human approval, context grounding, signed agent cards and exposing agent activity to users.
relevance: It shows that delegating to a peer agent opens a new trust boundary and needs identity, provenance and audit controls.

notes: The 'incident' label refers to a demonstrated attack technique; no exploitation was observed in the wild.

title: The 2026 MCP Roadmap
technologies: MCP; Streamable HTTP; DPoP; Workload Identity Federation
summary: MCP lead maintainer David Soria Parra published a 2026 roadmap organised around priority areas instead of release milestones, with Working Groups setting the timelines for their deliverables. The four priorities are: transport scalability (letting Streamable HTTP servers scale horizontally without holding state, plus .well-known metadata so capabilities can be discovered without a live connection); agent communication (retry and expiry semantics for the experimental SEP-1686 Tasks); governance maturation (a contributor ladder, and letting trusted Working Groups accept SEPs in their own domain); and enterprise readiness (audit trails, SSO-integrated auth, gateway behaviour and configuration portability), for which no dedicated Working Group exists yet. The post says no new official transports will be added this cycle and names SEP-1932 (DPoP) and SEP-1933 (Workload Identity Federation) among the proposals in review.
relevance: Stateless transport, task lifecycle and configuration portability are the protocol changes that most directly determine whether agent work can relocate between hosts.

title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
technologies: MCP; Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.0; Client ID Metadata Documents; MCP Apps
summary: MCP's lead maintainers released specification version 2026-07-28. It removes the initialize/initialized handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header, so each request carries its protocol version, client identity and capabilities in _meta, and an optional server/discover call is available. Server-to-client interactions such as elicitation and sampling are reworked as Multi Round-Trip Requests (SEP-2322), Streamable HTTP requests must send Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers (SEP-2243), and list responses carry ttlMs and cacheScope cache hints (SEP-2549). Authorization adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, binds client credentials to the issuing server, and formally deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents. Tasks move to an extension (SEP-2663), and Roots, Sampling, Logging and the legacy HTTP+SSE transport are deprecated with at least a twelve-month window.
relevance: A stateless core means no session needs to be migrated, so an MCP client or server can be relocated or load-balanced between requests, which simplifies runtime relocation.
